systems.name: Skeleton
systems.desc: Bones form the supporting framework of the body, protect organs, and provide attachment points for muscles. Their internal tissue also stores minerals and produces blood cells.

systems.name: Muscles
systems.desc: Skeletal muscles generate movement by pulling on their attachments. Together with tendons, they move joints, stabilize posture, and produce heat.

systems.name: Heart
systems.desc: The heart is a muscular pump with four chambers. Its valves direct blood forward through the pulmonary and systemic circuits.

systems.name: Sensory organs
systems.desc: These structures contribute to special senses, including sight, hearing, and balance. Their specialized tissues detect stimuli and work with the nervous system to convey information.

systems.name: Arteries
systems.desc: The heart drives blood through the circulation. Arteries carry blood away from the heart to supply tissues or, in the pulmonary circuit, to the lungs.

systems.name: Veins
systems.desc: Veins return blood toward the heart. Superficial and deep networks collect blood from the tissues; the pulmonary veins bring oxygenated blood back from the lungs.

systems.name: Nervous system
systems.desc: The brain, spinal cord, and peripheral nerves carry and process signals. They support sensation, movement, coordination, and automatic regulation of body functions.

systems.name: Respiratory
systems.desc: The airways conduct air to the lungs, where oxygen and carbon dioxide move between air and blood. Breathing depends on pressure changes produced by respiratory muscles.

systems.name: Digestive
systems.desc: The digestive tract breaks down food, absorbs nutrients and water, and moves waste onward. Accessory organs contribute bile and digestive enzymes.

systems.name: Urinary
systems.desc: The kidneys filter blood and regulate fluid, electrolyte, and acid-base balance. Urine travels through the ureters to the bladder and exits through the urethra.

systems.name: Lymphatic
systems.desc: Lymphatic vessels return excess tissue fluid to the circulation. Lymph nodes and other lymphoid organs support immune surveillance and responses.

systems.name: Endocrine
systems.desc: Endocrine organs release hormones into the blood to coordinate processes such as metabolism, growth, stress responses, and reproduction.

systems.name: Reproductive
systems.desc: The male reproductive structures represented here contribute to sperm production, maturation, transport, and the production of sex hormones.

systems.name: Body surface
systems.desc: The body surface provides an outer anatomical reference. The integumentary system forms a protective barrier and contributes to sensation and temperature regulation.

systems.name: Connective tissue
systems.desc: Cartilage, ligaments, and other connective tissues support, connect, and separate structures. Their roles include stabilizing joints and distributing mechanical loads.

explain.heart: A muscular pump in the chest. Its right side sends blood to the lungs; its left side sends blood through the systemic circulation.
explain.liver: A large organ beneath the right side of the diaphragm. It processes absorbed nutrients, produces bile, and synthesizes many proteins carried in the blood.
explain.brain: The central organ of the nervous system. Its interconnected regions support perception, movement, memory, language, and the regulation of bodily functions.
explain.stomach: A muscular chamber between the esophagus and small intestine. It stores and mixes food with acid and enzymes before releasing it into the duodenum.
explain.spleen: A lymphoid organ in the upper left abdomen. It filters blood, removes aging blood cells, and participates in immune responses.
explain.pancreas: An abdominal organ with digestive and endocrine roles. It supplies enzymes to the small intestine and releases hormones including insulin and glucagon.
explain.urinary bladder: A muscular reservoir in the pelvis that stores urine arriving from the kidneys through the ureters.
explain.trachea: The main airway connecting the larynx to the bronchi. Its cartilage supports keep the airway open during breathing.
explain.diaphragm: A broad muscle separating the chest and abdomen. When it contracts, it increases chest volume and helps draw air into the lungs.

ABDOMEN.note: Container structure; FMA9577 'abdomen' in BP3D is a bag of wall muscles + hip bones, not a surface. Linked to the 3D region instead.
ABDOMEN.name: Abdomen

ADRENAL_GLAND.name: Adrenal gland
ADRENAL_GLAND.definition: The suprarenal glands are flattened bodies capping the upper poles of the kidneys.

AMYGDALA.name: Amygdala
AMYGDALA.definition: The amygdala is an almond-shaped grey mass forming the roof and anterior wall of the tip of the inferior (temporal) horn of the lateral ventricle, deep to the uncus in the anteromedial temporal lobe, immediately anterosuperior to the head of the hippocampus.

AORTA.note: Whole aorta. The abdomen CT modules label only the abdominal segment (FMA3789); the whole vessel is shown so the correlation is not clipped.
AORTA.name: Abdominal aorta
AORTA.definition: The abdominal aorta begins at the aortic hiatus of the diaphragm and divides into the common iliac arteries.

AUTOCHTHONOUS_BACK_MUSCLE.note: TotalSegmentator 'autochthon' = erector spinae (iliocostalis, longissimus, spinalis) + semispinalis. BP3D has no single 'erector spinae' concept.
AUTOCHTHONOUS_BACK_MUSCLE.name: Deep back muscles
AUTOCHTHONOUS_BACK_MUSCLE.definition: The deep or intrinsic muscles of the back extend and rotate the vertebral column.

BRAIN.note: BP3D models gyri, nuclei, ventricles, brainstem and cerebellum, not a closed cerebral surface. Ventricles were mis-filed as 'cardiac' upstream and are relabelled nervous on import.
BRAIN.name: Brain

BRAINSTEM.note: Midbrain + pons + medulla oblongata (+ peduncles, colliculi).
BRAINSTEM.name: Brainstem
BRAINSTEM.definition: The brainstem comprises the midbrain, pons and medulla oblongata.

CAUDATE_NUCLEUS.name: Caudate nucleus
CAUDATE_NUCLEUS.definition: The caudate nucleus is an elongated arched mass of grey matter closely related to the lateral ventricle throughout its length.

CEREBELLAR_CORTEX.name: Cerebellar cortex
CEREBELLAR_CORTEX.definition: The cerebellar cortex is the thin grey mantle covering the cerebellum, thrown into closely set transverse folia, which pack a surface area of roughly half that of the cerebral cortex into about a tenth of the volume.
CEREBELLAR_CORTEX.reason: BP3D ships the cerebellum as one mesh (FMA67944); it is not split into cortex and white matter.

CEREBELLAR_WHITE_MATTER.name: Cerebellar white matter
CEREBELLAR_WHITE_MATTER.definition: The central white core of the cerebellum (corpus medullare), which sends a branching sheet into each folium; the branching pattern seen on a median section is termed the arbor vitae.
CEREBELLAR_WHITE_MATTER.reason: BP3D ships the cerebellum as one mesh (FMA67944); it is not split into cortex and white matter.

CEREBELLUM.name: Cerebellum
CEREBELLUM.definition: The cerebellum occupies the posterior cranial fossa below the tentorium cerebelli.

CEREBRAL_CORTEX.note: BP3D has named gyri and lobes, not a continuous cortical ribbon. Frontal-lobe cortex concepts + parietal/temporal/occipital lobes are combined.
CEREBRAL_CORTEX.name: Cerebral cortex
CEREBRAL_CORTEX.definition: The cerebral cortex is the layer of grey matter covering the surface of the cerebral hemispheres, thrown into folds forming the gyri, separated by sulci.

CEREBRAL_WHITE_MATTER.note: White matter of each hemisphere plus the internal capsules (FMA241998 alone omits the capsules its lateral children include).
CEREBRAL_WHITE_MATTER.name: Cerebral white matter
CEREBRAL_WHITE_MATTER.definition: The white matter of the cerebrum consists of myelinated fibres: projection, commissural and association.

CERVICAL_VERTEBRA.name: Cervical vertebra
CERVICAL_VERTEBRA.definition: The cervical vertebrae are the smallest of the movable vertebrae and bear foramina in their transverse processes.

CLAVICLE.name: Clavicle
CLAVICLE.definition: The clavicle forms the anterior portion of the shoulder girdle.

COLON.note: Cecum, ascending, transverse, descending colon and rectum. BP3D 4.0 isa set has no sigmoid colon mesh.
COLON.name: Colon
COLON.definition: The colon extends from the caecum to the rectum and is distinguished by its haustra and taeniae coli.

CORONA_RADIATA.name: Corona radiata
CORONA_RADIATA.definition: The corona radiata is the fan-shaped mass of projection fibres passing between the internal capsule and the cerebral cortex.
CORONA_RADIATA.reason: Not modelled in BP3D 4.0 (white matter is one mesh per hemisphere).

CORPUS_CALLOSUM.name: Corpus callosum
CORPUS_CALLOSUM.definition: The corpus callosum is the great transverse commissure uniting the cerebral hemispheres.

DUODENUM.name: Duodenum
DUODENUM.definition: The duodenum is the shortest, widest and most fixed part of the small intestine, curved around the head of the pancreas.

ESOPHAGUS.name: Oesophagus
ESOPHAGUS.definition: The oesophagus is a muscular canal passing from the pharynx through the posterior mediastinum to the stomach.

FEMUR.name: Femur
FEMUR.definition: The femur is the longest and strongest bone in the skeleton.

FIBULA.name: Fibula
FIBULA.definition: The fibula is the slender lateral bone of the leg, bearing little weight but giving attachment to muscles and forming the lateral malleolus at the ankle.

FOOT.note: Skeleton of the foot (26 bones per side); the CT module's 'Foot' is the whole region.
FOOT.name: Foot

FORNIX.name: Fornix
FORNIX.definition: The fornix is a longitudinal, arch-shaped lamella of white substance situated below the corpus callosum, consisting of two symmetrical bands, one for either hemisphere.

FOURTH_VENTRICLE.note: Mis-filed as 'cardiac' upstream; relabelled nervous on import.
FOURTH_VENTRICLE.name: Fourth ventricle
FOURTH_VENTRICLE.definition: The fourth ventricle lies between the pons and medulla in front and the cerebellum behind.

FRONTAL_LOBE.name: Frontal lobe
FRONTAL_LOBE.definition: The frontal lobe lies in front of the central sulcus and above the lateral fissure.

GALLBLADDER.name: Gallbladder
GALLBLADDER.definition: The gallbladder is a pear-shaped reservoir for bile lodged in a fossa on the under surface of the liver.

GLOBUS_PALLIDUS.name: Globus pallidus
GLOBUS_PALLIDUS.definition: The globus pallidus is the medial, paler part of the lentiform nucleus.

GLUTEAL_MUSCLE.name: Gluteal muscles
GLUTEAL_MUSCLE.definition: The gluteal muscles extend, abduct and rotate the thigh at the hip joint.

HAND.note: Skeleton of the hand; the CT module's 'Hand' is the whole region.
HAND.name: Hand

HAND_BONE.note: Carpal bones + metacarpals + phalanges of the fingers.
HAND_BONE.name: Bone of the hand
HAND_BONE.definition: The skeleton of the hand comprises the eight carpal bones of the wrist, five metacarpals, and fourteen phalanges - two in the thumb and three in each of the other digits.

HEART.note: BP3D 4.0 isa set models chamber cavities, atrial walls, one ventricular wall and the valve leaflets; there is no single closed heart surface.
HEART.name: Heart
HEART.definition: The heart is a hollow muscular organ enclosed in the pericardium, occupying the middle mediastinum.

HIPPOCAMPUS.name: Hippocampus
HIPPOCAMPUS.definition: The hippocampus is a curved elevation of grey matter in the floor of the temporal horn of the lateral ventricle.

HIP_BONE.name: Hip bone
HIP_BONE.definition: The hip bone is a large flattened irregular bone formed by the ilium, ischium and pubis.

ILIAC_ARTERY.name: Iliac artery
ILIAC_ARTERY.definition: The common iliac arteries arise from the aortic bifurcation and divide into external and internal iliac arteries.

ILIAC_VEIN.name: Iliac vein
ILIAC_VEIN.definition: The common iliac veins unite to form the inferior vena cava.

ILIOPSOAS.name: Iliopsoas
ILIOPSOAS.definition: The iliacus and psoas major act together as the chief flexor of the thigh at the hip.

INFERIOR_VENA_CAVA.name: Inferior vena cava
INFERIOR_VENA_CAVA.definition: The inferior vena cava returns blood from the lower half of the body to the right atrium.

INSULA.name: Insula
INSULA.definition: The insula is the cortex buried in the depth of the lateral fissure, covered by the opercula.

INTERNAL_CAPSULE.name: Internal capsule
INTERNAL_CAPSULE.definition: The internal capsule is a broad band of white matter between the caudate nucleus and thalamus medially and the lentiform nucleus laterally.

KIDNEY.name: Kidney
KIDNEY.definition: The kidneys are situated in the posterior part of the abdomen, one on either side of the vertebral column, behind the peritoneum.

LATERAL_VENTRICLE.note: Mis-filed as 'cardiac' upstream; relabelled nervous on import.
LATERAL_VENTRICLE.name: Lateral ventricle
LATERAL_VENTRICLE.definition: The lateral ventricles are two irregular cavities within the cerebral hemispheres, communicating with the third ventricle through the interventricular foramina.

LIVER.note: BP3D 4.0 isa set has NO liver surface mesh: only the caudate lobe, the biliary tree and the intrahepatic vessels. Shown as related structures.
LIVER.name: Liver
LIVER.definition: The liver is the largest gland in the body, occupying the right hypochondrium and extending into the epigastrium.

LOWER_LIMB.note: Skeleton of the lower limb; the CT knee module's 'Lower limb' is the whole region.
LOWER_LIMB.name: Lower limb

LOWER_LOBE_LEFT.note: No lobe surface in BP3D 4.0 isa set; the lobe's segmental bronchial tree is shown as related.
LOWER_LOBE_LEFT.name: Lower lobe of left lung
LOWER_LOBE_LEFT.definition: The lower lobe of the left lung lies posteroinferior to the oblique fissure.

LOWER_LOBE_RIGHT.note: No lobe surface in BP3D 4.0 isa set; the lobe's segmental bronchial tree is shown as related.
LOWER_LOBE_RIGHT.name: Lower lobe of right lung
LOWER_LOBE_RIGHT.definition: The lower lobe of the right lung lies below and behind the oblique fissure.

LUMBAR_VERTEBRA.name: Lumbar vertebra
LUMBAR_VERTEBRA.definition: The lumbar vertebrae are the largest segments of the movable part of the vertebral column.

LUNG.note: No lung surface in BP3D 4.0 isa set; the bronchial tree is shown as related.
LUNG.name: Lung
LUNG.definition: The lungs are the essential organs of respiration, occupying the pleural cavities on either side of the mediastinum. Each is conical, with an apex reaching above the first rib and a concave base resting on the diaphragm.

METATARSAL.name: Metatarsal bone
METATARSAL.definition: The five metatarsal bones are long bones lying between the tarsus and the phalanges, forming the skeleton of the forefoot.

MIDDLE_LOBE_RIGHT.note: No lobe surface in BP3D 4.0 isa set; the lobe's segmental bronchial tree is shown as related.
MIDDLE_LOBE_RIGHT.name: Middle lobe of right lung
MIDDLE_LOBE_RIGHT.definition: The middle lobe of the right lung is a wedge lying between the horizontal and oblique fissures.

NUCLEUS_ACCUMBENS.name: Nucleus accumbens
NUCLEUS_ACCUMBENS.definition: A grey mass lying where the head of the caudate nucleus and the putamen become continuous beneath the anterior limb of the internal capsule, forming the ventral part of the striatum.

OCCIPITAL_LOBE.name: Occipital lobe
OCCIPITAL_LOBE.definition: The occipital lobe forms the posterior extremity of the cerebral hemisphere, behind the parieto-occipital sulcus.

PANCREAS.name: Pancreas
PANCREAS.definition: The pancreas is a compound racemose gland lying transversely across the posterior abdominal wall behind the stomach.

PARANASAL_SINUS.name: Paranasal sinus
PARANASAL_SINUS.definition: The paranasal sinuses are air-filled cavities within the frontal, maxillary, ethmoid and sphenoid bones, communicating with the nasal cavity and lined by mucous membrane. The mastoid air cells of the temporal bone are similarly pneumatised.
PARANASAL_SINUS.reason: BP3D models bones, not air spaces; no maxillary/frontal/sphenoid/ethmoid sinus cavities exist in the isa set.

PARIETAL_LOBE.name: Parietal lobe
PARIETAL_LOBE.definition: The parietal lobe lies behind the central sulcus and in front of the parieto-occipital sulcus.

PELVIS.note: Container structure. The bony pelvis (FMA16580 = both hip bones + sacrum) is reachable through HIP_BONE and SACRUM.
PELVIS.name: Pelvis

PHALANX_FOOT.name: Phalanx of foot
PHALANX_FOOT.definition: The phalanges of the foot are fourteen in number, three for each of the lesser toes and two for the great toe.

PORTAL_VEIN.name: Portal vein
PORTAL_VEIN.definition: The portal vein conveys blood from the abdominal digestive tract and spleen to the liver.

PROSTATE.name: Prostate
PROSTATE.definition: The prostate is a firm glandular body surrounding the commencement of the male urethra.

PUTAMEN.name: Putamen
PUTAMEN.definition: The putamen is the outer and larger part of the striatum, separated from the globus pallidus by a lamina of white matter.

RIB.name: Rib
RIB.definition: The ribs are elastic arches of bone forming the greater part of the thoracic skeleton. They are twelve in number on either side, articulating behind with the vertebral column.

SACRUM.name: Sacrum
SACRUM.definition: The sacrum is a large triangular bone formed by the union of five vertebrae, wedged between the two hip bones.

SKULL.note: Cranial + facial bones (the upstream concept also lists eyeball parts, filtered out here).
SKULL.name: Skull
SKULL.definition: The skull is the skeleton of the head, comprising the cranium, which encloses the brain, and the mandible. Its bones are united by sutures except at the temporomandibular joint.

SMALL_BOWEL.note: Jejunum + ileum. Duodenum is its own structure.
SMALL_BOWEL.name: Small intestine
SMALL_BOWEL.definition: The jejunum and ileum form the mesenteric portion of the small intestine, suspended by the mesentery.

SPINAL_CORD.name: Spinal cord
SPINAL_CORD.definition: The spinal cord is the elongated part of the central nervous system occupying the upper two-thirds of the vertebral canal.

SPLEEN.name: Spleen
SPLEEN.definition: The spleen is a highly vascular organ situated in the left hypochondrium between the fundus of the stomach and the diaphragm.

STERNUM.name: Sternum
STERNUM.definition: The sternum is a flat narrow bone forming the middle of the anterior wall of the thorax, consisting of the manubrium, the body and the xiphoid process.

STOMACH.name: Stomach
STOMACH.definition: The stomach is the most dilated part of the digestive tube, lying between the oesophagus and the duodenum.

SUBARACHNOID_SPACE.name: Subarachnoid space
SUBARACHNOID_SPACE.definition: The subarachnoid space lies between the arachnoid mater and the pia mater and contains cerebrospinal fluid.
SUBARACHNOID_SPACE.reason: BP3D models parenchyma and vessels, not CSF spaces.

TARSAL.name: Tarsal bone
TARSAL.definition: The tarsus consists of seven bones - the calcaneus, talus, navicular, cuboid and three cuneiforms - forming the posterior half of the foot and the ankle.

TELENCEPHALON.note: Gyri, lobes, basal ganglia, white matter; no closed hemispheric surface.
TELENCEPHALON.name: Telencephalon

TEMPORAL_LOBE.name: Temporal lobe
TEMPORAL_LOBE.definition: The temporal lobe lies below the lateral fissure and extends back to the occipital lobe.

THALAMUS.name: Thalamus
THALAMUS.definition: The thalamus is a large ovoid mass of grey matter forming much of the lateral wall of the third ventricle.

THIRD_VENTRICLE.note: Mis-filed as 'cardiac' upstream; relabelled nervous on import.
THIRD_VENTRICLE.name: Third ventricle
THIRD_VENTRICLE.definition: The third ventricle is a narrow median cleft between the two thalami.

THORACIC_VERTEBRA.name: Thoracic vertebra
THORACIC_VERTEBRA.definition: The thoracic vertebrae are twelve in number and are distinguished by the costal facets on the sides of their bodies for articulation with the heads of the ribs.

TIBIA.name: Tibia
TIBIA.definition: The tibia is the medial and larger of the two bones of the leg, transmitting the weight of the body from the femur to the foot.

TORSO.note: Container structure of the living-patient torso modules.
TORSO.name: Torso

UPPER_LOBE_LEFT.note: No lobe surface in BP3D 4.0 isa set; the lobe's segmental bronchial tree is shown as related.
UPPER_LOBE_LEFT.name: Upper lobe of left lung
UPPER_LOBE_LEFT.definition: The left lung is divided by the oblique fissure into an upper and a lower lobe; the upper lobe includes the lingula.

URINARY_BLADDER.name: Urinary bladder
URINARY_BLADDER.definition: The urinary bladder is a musculomembranous reservoir for urine situated in the pelvis behind the pubic symphysis.

VENTRAL_DIENCEPHALON.note: SynthSeg's composite 'ventral DC' has no FMA equivalent; hypothalamus + diencephalon parts are shown.
VENTRAL_DIENCEPHALON.name: Ventral diencephalic / subthalamic region (composite)
VENTRAL_DIENCEPHALON.definition: NOT a single named structure and NOT a Terminologia Anatomica term: this is the FreeSurfer "ventral diencephalon" segmentation label, a composite of the grey and white matter packed between the thalamus above, the internal capsule laterally and the midbrain below. It contains the hypothalamus, mammillary body and subthalamic nucleus (diencephalic), the geniculate bodies (metathalamic), the substantia nigra and red nucleus (which are MIDBRAIN, not diencephalon), the zona incerta, and fibre bundles including the medial lemniscus and lenticular fasciculus. It is shown as an aggregate because this segmentation cannot separate them: do not learn any one of these structures from this pin.

VERTEBRAL_CANAL.name: Vertebral canal
VERTEBRAL_CANAL.definition: The vertebral canal is formed by the vertebral foramina in series and contains the spinal cord with its meninges and vessels.
VERTEBRAL_CANAL.reason: A space, not a structure, in BP3D. Use SPINAL_CORD and the vertebrae.
